If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% for mid horizon (8–14 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon (15–30 days) to capture momentum.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon (15–30 days) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, apply a ±0.5% adjustment to forecast based on most recent sentiment direction, with higher weight on last 2 days.
